claims.summary: Observed: scan_known_model_control_markers (L114-144) is non-destructive and distinguishes markers used as grammatical subjects from merely-present ones.
claims.disposition: Verified from complete source dialogue_runtime.rs@902a0358 L114-144: scan builds a `remainder` String + `matches` Vec and never mutates input; a marker's bytes reach remainder ONLY when reference_syntax.is_some() (L129-131), otherwise the bytes are dropped. reference_syntax (L49-60) classifies via delimiter syntax OR followed_by_explicit_exact_token_relation. Description is accurate; no change.

claims.summary: Observed: exact_reference_delimiter_syntax (L199-229) maps quotation/grouping styles including multi-byte CJK pairs like the corner brackets.
claims.disposition: Verified with one grounded clarification: the pair table lives in exact_reference_delimiter_pair (L153-197), which exact_reference_delimiter_syntax (L199-229) calls. The corner pair (L168) is in the QUOTED block, so a corner-bracketed marker resolves to QuotedExactKnownToken, not grouped; the lenticular pair (L182) is grouped. Pinned by existing test exact_reference_delimiter_syntax_classifies_cjk_corner_quoted_and_lenticular_grouped at the same source SHA. No grammar change.

claims.summary: Likely Snag: first_word_after (L89-96) may behave inconsistently for markers followed by a newline/tab or a complex punctuation cluster before the next word.
claims.disposition: Grounded, non-manifesting. first_word_after does text[end..].split_whitespace() (space/tab/newline uniform), trims each chunk to alnum/underscore, then find(non-empty) — punctuation-only chunks skipped, true next word found regardless of intervening whitespace/punctuation. Pinned by existing tests grounds_first_word_after_punctuation_boundary/_non_breaking_space/_internal_soft_hyphen/_attached_double_dash + preserves_relation_across_newline. Concern preserved; no bug.

claims.summary: Likely Snag: max_by_key(|t| t.len()) in longest_exact_known_model_control_marker_at (L97-112) could cause greedy shadowing if two markers share a prefix and the shorter is the intended unit.
claims.disposition: Grounded + newly pinned. KNOWN_MODEL_CONTROL_MARKERS (fallback_contracts.rs L159-180) has NO marker that is a proper byte-prefix of another, so at most one marker starts at any offset and max_by_key never disambiguates a prefix shadow — greedy shadowing is structurally unreachable for the current set. Added focused test known_model_control_markers_have_no_proper_prefix_shadow asserting that invariant + isolated-match behavior; a future prefix-overlapping marker would fail it.

claims.summary: One Test Each #1 (Contextual Preservation): a marker followed by "denotes" stays in remainder (L130) because followed_by_explicit_exact_token_relation (L64-86) returns true.
claims.disposition: Outcome verified, mechanism corrected. `denotes` IS in the relation allowlist (L71), so unbracketed `<marker> denotes` is preserved via ExplicitExactKnownTokenRelation. BUT for her bracketed [MARKER] form, reference_syntax checks exact_reference_delimiter_syntax FIRST (L50-52) -> preserved via GroupedExactKnownToken, not the relation path. Committed scan_known_model_control_markers_quoted_context_precedes_following_relation_verb pins this precedence at the same SHA.
